REASONS .9. POINT No.1:
Before proceeding further in this case, it is relevant to note admitted and undisputed facts in this case.
The respondent No.1 Smt.

Veeramma, R.N. Nanjundappa, Sarvamangalamma and Shashipratap are the joint owners of the property bearing Survey No.46/1A1A1 measuring to an extent of 1117 Square Meters of Huskurkodi village and the said property has been acquired for widening of NH-4 under Preliminary Notification dated 18.12.2006 and Final Notification dated 14.11.2007, is an admitted fact.

It is also an admitted and undisputed fact in this case that the respondent No.3/Special Land Acquisition and Competent Authority of National Highways Authority of India being a SLAO determined the compensation at Rs.247.10 per Square meter for the acquired land.

sentences.text: Subsequent to the receipt of compensation or passing of the award, the respondent No.1 has filed the application 02.09.2009 for enhancing the compensation at the rate of Rs.2,000/- per Square feet.
Accordingly, the application is taken by the respondent No.2 for consideration.

On basis of the said application,
the respondent No. 2 held an inquiry and passed common order in LAQ/ARB/NH-4 (BET) 03/2010-11 dated 09.02.2021.

The respondent No. 2 in its order enhanced the compensation at Rs.1186/- per Square meter i.e., guidance value of NH lands abutting National Highway is Rs. 1186/- per Square meter and the respondent No.2 added 50% and 25% on the guidance value and also the SLAO determined and paid the compensation per Square meter is Rs.2,075/- per Square meter (50% of Rs.1186/-
= Rs. 593/- + 25% of Rs. 1186/- = Rs.296/- + 1186)
as respondent No. 3 determined the compensation in respect of agricultural land)
The said enhancement has been challenged by the petitioner in this petition.

The grievance of the petitioner is that the respondent No.2 without considering the relevant provisions of National Highways Act and also without considering the guidance value or market value of the property as on the date of Preliminary Notification enhanced the compensation by relying on the guidance value of the year 2007 published vide notification bearing No.
CVC/BUD/5/2006-07 dated 17.04.2007.
The petitioner also claimed that the Preliminary Notification was published as on 18.12.2006.
As such, the respondent No. 2 ought to have considered the market value of the property of the year 2006 and not of the year 2007.
As the aforesaid notification relied by the Arbitrator came to effect from 17.04.2007 i.e., after lapse of more than 4 months from the date of publication of Preliminary Notification.
Accordingly claimed that the said enhancement cannot be accepted.
It is true that as per the NH Act, the market value of the A.P. No.145/2021 land as on the date of Preliminary Notification has to be considered.

.12. The petitioner also claimed that whatever the document relied by the respondent No. 2 for enhancing the compensation is not brought to the notice of the petitioner before passing the award/judgment.
Accordingly, claimed that such award is liable to be set aside as per Section 24 of National Highways Authority Act.

In this context, the petitioner relied on the decision reported in (2019) 15 SCC 131 in a case of Ssangyong Engineering and Construction Company Limited Vs.
National Highways Authority of India.

sentences.text: It is true that in the said decision, the Hon'ble Supreme Court held that whatever the document relied by the Arbitrator shall be brought to the notice of the parties, so that the parties can make submission or give a rebuttal evidence about such documents.
However, in the case on hand, such notification is not found in the record received from the Arbitrator.

It is the claim of the petitioner in the petition that as per the Special Instructions to the notification dated 17.04.2007 regarding the fixing of estimated market value, the market value to be fixed in respect of the acquired property.

The instructions dated 17.04.2007 provides that the properties adjacent to National and State Highways for which rates have not been fixed in the rate list, additional rate of 50% and 25% of other properties shall be fixed respectively National Highways Authority Of India vs Veeramma on 2 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/172344382/
5 and claimed that if the rate is not fixed for the properties adjacent to the properties of National Highways, the Arbitrator can enhance the price at 50% and in case of State Highways, additional rate of 25% can be fixed but 75% cannot be enhanced.

sentences.text: The claim of the petitioner is that the Arbitrator / respondent No. 2 enhanced 75% of the market value, which is permissible and accordingly claimed that the enhancement cannot be accepted.
Admittedly, the SLAO fixed the market value to the acquired property is Rs.1186/- per Square Meters and that has been enhanced to Rs.2,075/- per Square A.P. No.145/2021 Meters.
If the said enhancement is accepted, certainly it is clear that the respondent No. 2 enhanced the market value which is 4 times of the market value determined by the LAO.
Hence, it is for the Arbitrator to give reasons on what basis such enhancement was ordered.
.14. The only reason assigned by the respondent No. 2 for enhancement of 75% is the discretion.
Now it is well settled principle of law that discretion must be used in judicially and not arbitrarily.

Admittedly as observed by the respondent No. 2 in its order as well as claimed by the petitioner in the petition that the Arbitrator can enhance 50% of the market value, if the market value of the acquired property besides National Highways is not found in or fixed in the rate list.
As such, only 50% of the market value can be enhanced by the SLAO and not more than that.
If at all the Arbitrator is enhancing another 25%, that is totally 75%, then there must be special reasons why the Arbitrator is enhancing 25% of the market value.
Such A.P. No.145/2021 reasons are not found in the order of the Arbitrator / respondent No. 2.
When such a case, certainly said enhancement cannot be accepted.

It is also not made out by the respondent No. 2 in its order that the property of respondent No. 1 has been acquired for which the rate is not fixed or not found in the rate list so that he has added 50% holding that the property is adjacent to national highway along with additional rate with 25%.
Further the value of the property has been enhanced as per the notification of the year 2007, which is also not the part of records received from the Arbitrator.
Further, no such case is made out by the respondent No. 1 before the respondent No. 2 in the Arbitration proceedings.

.15. Apart from that 50% or 25% of the enhancement as prescribed under the Special Instructions applicable to all offices regarding valuation at condition No. 2 is not applicable to the property for which market value has been determined.
As per the documents produced by the petitioner at Annexure-B at A.P. No.145/2021 page No. 21 the guidance value of property has been fixed.

As such condition No. 2, which reads as "The properties adjacent to National and State Highways for which rates have not been fixed in the rate list, additional rate at 50% and 25% of other properties shall be fixed respectively" is not applicable to the facts of this case because the value of the property has been already fixed in the rate list.

.16. Therefore, it is clear that the award passed by the Arbitrator is patently illegal and against the statutory provisions of Substantive Law that is in force and the award passed by the Arbitrator also leads to draw adverse inference under Section 24 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act as the documents relied by the Arbitrator not found in the records received from the Arbitrator.

The Arbitrator relied on the guidance value of the year 2007 that came to effect from 01.04.2007 and the land involved in this acquired one year prior to the said date and also the Arbitrator has not given any specific reason for enhancement of 25% A.P. No.145/2021 as claimed in the year.

As such,
certainly the award passed by the Arbitrator is patently illegal.

It is well settled principle of law that National Highways Authority Of India vs Veeramma on 2 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/172344382/
6

sentences.text: if the award passed by the Arbitrator is patently illegal, then such award should be set aside.

As discussed earlier, as the respondent No. 1 though supported the award passed by the Arbitrator /
respondent No. 2 has not placed any materials to substantiate enhancement made by the Arbitrator to the acquired property.
.17. Now it is for the consideration of this court to see that whether the said enhancement is supported with any materials or is there any reasons given by the Arbitrator for the said enhancement.

It appears from the award that the Arbitrator enhanced the compensation on the basis of notification bearing No. CVC/BUD/5/2006-07 dated 17.04.2007 which is subsequent to the preliminary notification.

On perusal of records of arbitration proceedings, it is clear that the notification bearing No. CVC/BUD/5/2006-07 dated 17.04.2007 is not the part of record and also there is no A.P. No.145/2021 material on record to show that said notification has been brought to the notice of petitioner before passing of the Award.

In view of the principle laid down by Apex court in a case of Ssangyong Engineering and Construction Company Limited Vs. National Highways Authority of India such award cannot be accepted as the notification relied by the Arbitrator is not the part of arbitration proceedings and the same has not been brought to the notice of petitioner before passing the award.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As such opportunity to the petitioner to make submission or give explanation to the said notification has been denied.
As such, certainly this enhancement of respondent No.2/arbitrator cannot be accepted.

.18. In the case on hand, the respondent No.1(b),
(d) and (e) appeared before the Court.

Though the respondent No.1(a)(c), respondents 2 and 3 served with the notice not chosen to appear before the court to resist the case of the petitioner or to support the award passed by the respondent No.3.
Absolutely there is no material placed before the court to disbelieve the A.P. No.145/2021 petitioner case or to substantiate the award passed by the respondent No.3.
Hence, this Court is of the humble opinion that the petitioner has made out sufficient grounds to intervene with the award passed by the Arbitrator and the award is liable to be set aside.
Accordingly, the point No.1 is held in the affirmative.

In the result, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER Petition filed under Section 34(2) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act,
1996 is hereby allowed.

Consequently, the award passed by the Arbitrator / respondent No. 2 in case No.
LAQ/ARB/NH-4 (BET)03/2010-11 dated 09.02.2021 pertaining to Sy. No.46/1A1A1 measuring 1117 Sq. Meters of Huskurkodi village, K.R. Puram Taluk, is set aside with a liberty to the parties to pursue their remedy in accordance with law.
A.P. No.145/2021 Office is directed to send back the Lower Court Records.
